## INCIDENT REPORT: Win32/Koi Stealer Infection

**Incident ID:** MTA-2024-09-04  
**Analysis Date:** 2024-09-04  
**Evidence File:** 2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap

### INFECTED HOST IDENTIFICATION

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **IPv4 Address** | 172.17.0.99 |
| **MAC Address** | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 |
| **Windows Hostname** | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT |
| **Workgroup/Domain** | BEPOSITIVE |
| **Logged-In User Account** | Not captured in network traffic (domain-joined workstation, BEPOSITIVE\\*) |

### MALWARE IDENTIFICATION

**Family Name:** Win32/Koi Stealer  
**Attribution Confidence:** Signature-confirmed (ETPRO TROJAN alert)  
**Detection Rule:** ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2

### INDICATORS OF COMPROMISE (GROUNDED IN TRAFFIC)

**Command-and-Control Endpoint:**
- **IP Address:** 79.124.78.197
- **Port:** 80 (HTTP)
- **Protocol:** HTTP/1.1

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` (POST requests, recurring beacons every ~60 seconds, payload ~40 bytes)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` (POST requests, payload ~105 bytes)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` (GET reconnaissance request with session identifier `qIOuKk7U`)

**HTTP Indicators:**
- User-Agent: Spoofed IE7.0 (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0...`)
- Method: POST (data exfiltration/command polling), GET (reconnaissance)
- Content-Type: Binary data (encoded/obfuscated payloads)

**File Names:** None extracted or observed in transfer

**File Hashes:** No executable files transferred observed in captured traffic; beaconing traffic only contains encrypted/binary payloads

### ATTACK TIMELINE

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|-----------|-------|
| 2024-09-04 17:32 | DNS NXDOMAIN responses, LDAP queries to BEPOSITIVE domain infrastructure |
| 2024-09-04 17:33 | SMB exploitation attempt: NTMLSSP unicode ASN.1 overflow (port 139) |
| 2024-09-04 17:33 | SMB lateral movement probing: IPC$ share enumeration, SMB_COM_TRANSACTION exploitation |
| 2024-09-04 17:34 | Kerberos RPC principal name overflow attack attempt (port 88) |
| 2024-09-04 17:35 | First HTTP POST to C2 at 79.124.78.197/foots.php (initial callback) |
| 2024-09-04 17:35+ | Recurring C2 beacons to /foots.php and /index.php (interval ~60 seconds, persistent for >1 hour) |

### ATTACK SUMMARY

The Windows 10 workstation (DESKTOP-RNVO9AT) was infected with Win32/Koi Stealer, a credential-stealing malware family. The infection demonstrates multi-stage exploitation: initial SMB/Kerberos probing against local domain infrastructure (BEPOSITIVE), followed by successful code execution and persistent HTTP-based command-and-control communication. The C2 beaconing pattern (regular POST heartbeats to /foots.php with 60-second intervals, interspersed with GET reconnaissance queries) is consistent with data exfiltration and remote command execution capabilities. No file hash indicators are available from the traffic capture, as command-and-control communication occurred entirely over HTTP with binary-encoded payloads.
